events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
Safety screen [F6][SAFE-1]: the complaint alleges dangerous driving — speeding, hard braking "the whole way", shoulder overtaking, "I was scared and felt unsafe" — which is a dangerous-driving allegation squarely within SAFE-2 and also a safety incident by its own filing; the driver's written statement calls the rider "stupid", hostile language aimed at the other party, which is abuse under SAFE-1. Both are recorded by me in safety_concern/safety_basis, and the trace settles SAFE-1 as a safety incident with no automatic ruling permitted [F6].

The chat adds no in-trip safety report: two messages, all timestamped, are pickup coordination only — the rider's location message [F3] and the driver's ETA reply [F4] — read as a normal polite exchange [F5][SAFE-1]. That silence is a genuine weakness of the rider's account but it does not cancel the escalation the clause requires.

The system records neither confirm nor refute the driving allegation: actual 10.5 km vs 10.6 km optimal and 15.9 min vs 16.5 min estimated [F1][F2] show no distance or time gained, which is consistent with an uneventful trip, but absence of a speed/braking record is not a finding of safe driving [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. No traffic facts exist for this case, so RD-4 never arises.

Because the case is a safety incident and my screen is at least "suspected", I do not rule on the merits and issue no amount (amount is null) [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. The human reviewer should look at: the rider's dangerous-driving complaint; the complete timestamped chat [F3][F4][F5]; the driver's post-trip statement [F6]; and the absence of any speed, braking, lane or incident telemetry, so the allegation is neither corroborated nor disproved. Both profiles show 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days [F7][F8], so no account flag is warranted and none is set.

Nothing in my ruling is contested by either side's revised ask: both advocate briefs and rebuttals end at escalate.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint is a dangerous-driving allegation ("speeding and braking hard the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder. I was scared and felt unsafe"), which is a SAFE-2 trigger: the case must go to a person and no automated ruling may be issued on it.

The driver's own written statement calls the rider "stupid" (F6), an insult directed at the passenger recorded in the case file, which is abuse/harassment language requiring escalation under SAFE-1 rather than an automated disposition.

The chat record is complete — 2 messages, every one timestamped (F5) — and neither message contains any complaint, concern or report from the rider about the driving during the trip, so the file contains no contemporaneous chat corroboration of the safety allegation.

The two neutral messages that do exist (F3: rider advises her location and blue shirt at 08:29; F4: driver replies "On my way, about 6 min, blue Toyota Prius" at 08:30) show a normal, polite pickup exchange and give the driver no basis for the insult in F6.

Nothing in the rider's own record explains or justifies the driver's hostile remark: rider account is 1447 days old, rating 4.78–4.8, with 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes in 90 days (F7), so the driver's "stupid" characterisation in F6 is unsupported by any prior conduct record.

The driver has 705 trips in the last 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F8); this supports sending the account for review (flag_account as an additional action) so that repeated unsafe-driving or abusive-conduct patterns, if any, are examined by Ryde rather than treated as an isolated automated finding.

weaknesses: There is no GPS, timeline or fare record of speeding, hard braking or shoulder-overtaking in this file: the only route figures are F1 (actual 10.5 km vs optimal 10.6 km, -1%) and F2 (15.9 min vs 16.5 min estimated), which are consistent with a normal, non-reckless trip, so the rider's account in the complaint is uncorroborated by system records.

The driver's insult in F6 is directed at the rider in a post-trip written statement rather than being a threat or an act of harassment during the ride, so the judge may read it as rude rather than as a SAFE-1 safety concern; the rider's own chat (F3, F4) is entirely neutral and complains of nothing.

Profile facts F7/F8 cut both ways: both parties have 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days, so neither side's history independently supports the safety allegation; F8 can only support the additional flag_account request, never the main finding.

claims.assertion: The rider's speeding/hard-braking/shoulder-overtaking complaint is not corroborated by any system record: the GPS track shows the trip took 15.9 min against a 16.5 min estimate and 10.5 km against a 10.6 km optimal route, i.e. no time or distance was gained at all (F1, F2), and the trip record contains no traffic, incident or speed evidence (no traffic facts returned for this case).

The written driver statement says the rider 'is stupid and was on the phone the whole trip. I drove normally' (F6); the abusive word 'stupid' is the driver's own post-trip remark about the rider, not a threat, intimidation or harassment directed at the rider during the trip, so it does not by itself trigger SAFE-1.

The in-app chat is complete and fully timestamped (2 messages, both timestamped, F5) and contains only pickup coordination — the rider's location message at 08:29 (F3) and the driver's ETA reply at 08:30 (F4) — with no complaint about driving, no request to slow down or stop, and no safety message from the rider at any point.

The driver's account has 1434 days (3.9 y) of history, a 4.78 rating over 705 trips in the last 90 days, and zero disputes and zero upheld complaints in 90 days (F8); this profile supports no flag_account request and shows no pattern of dangerous driving.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint alleges overtaking on the shoulder (dangerous driving); under SAFE-2 any dangerous-driving allegation escalates the case to a person regardless of my rebuttal, so the outcome may be escalation rather than no_action (F1, F2).

The driver's own statement calls the rider 'stupid' (F6); a judge may read that as abuse/harassment of a rider and route the case to a person under SAFE-1, and it is a bad look even though it was written after the trip and not sent to the rider via chat (F5, F6).

There is no in-trip telemetry in the fact set — no speed, braking or lane-position record — so I cannot positively prove the driving was smooth; my case rests on the absence of corroboration (F1, F2, no traffic facts) plus trip timing (F2), which a judge may treat as 'undetermined' rather than proof of safe driving.

points.response: I do not contest that F1 and F2 show no distance or time was gained (10.5 km vs 10.6 km optimal; 15.9 min vs 16.5 min estimated), but the absence of a speeding/braking record is not a finding that the driving was safe: SAFE-2 makes a dangerous-driving allegation escalate to a person precisely because the automated record set cannot resolve it, and the rider's complaint is exactly such an allegation.

The rider does not need 'stupid' alone to carry the case: the contested item is the dangerous-driving allegation, which escalates under SAFE-2 on its own; F6 ('The rider is stupid and was on the phone the whole trip. I drove normally') is additional material that a person — not an automated ruling — should read alongside the complaint, since SAFE-1 requires the judge to screen every case for abuse language in chat, complaint or driver statement.

I agree the chat is complete and timestamped and contains no in-trip complaint (F3, F4, F5); that silence is a genuine weakness of the rider's case, but it is also a reason for human review rather than for a clean no_action on an uncorroborated dangerous-driving allegation under SAFE-2.

F8 (1434 days, 4.78 rating, 705 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) indeed gives no pattern, so I no longer press flag_account as a requested action and rely on it for nothing; the driver's clean 90-day window is conceded, and it does not convert the rider's allegation into a no_action finding.

Conceded only as to routing: a dangerous-driving allegation does go to a person, but the escalation must carry the fact that the two system records that exist are exculpatory, not merely neutral — actual 10.5 km vs 10.6 km optimal (F1) and 15.9 min vs 16.5 min estimated (F2) mean the driver finished shorter and faster than the quoted route, which is inconsistent with the rider's 'the whole way' speeding claim grabbing any time, so the summary sent to the human reviewer should record 'allegation unsupported by system records', not an implied finding.

The word 'stupid' in F6 appears in a post-trip written statement, not in any message sent to the rider — the complete, fully timestamped chat (F5) contains no abusive word at all, so there is no harassment of the rider 'of any kind' during the ride to escalate under SAFE-1; at most the remark is rude, and it is not a threat, intimidation, sexual advance or assault of the kind SAFE-1 lists.

I agree the chat is complete and silent on the driving, and I rely on the same fact for a different conclusion: a rider who 'was scared and felt unsafe' the whole way had two uninterrupted opportunities to say so in-app and said nothing (F3, F4, F5), and the rider never asked the driver to slow down or stop — so the file lacks the contemporaneous corroboration SAFE-1 looks for (F5).

Accepted: F3 and F4 are a normal pickup exchange, and my case does not rest on the rider's messages but on the absence of any system record contradicting a normal trip (F1, F2) and the completeness of the chat (F5) — nothing in F3 or F4 describes speeding, hard braking or shoulder-overtaking.

F7 does not support the rider's safety allegation at all: the rider's profile shows 1447 d account age, rating 4.8 and 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 days (F7), i.e. no behaviour record — good or bad — that explains or corroborates the claim of reckless driving, and the rider's own complaint is the only source of the driving allegation.

F8 does not support a flag_account request: 705 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F8) is the opposite of the 'repeated or severe' pattern required, and the policy expressly says profile facts are an additional-action basis only, never the main finding — the same rule defeats the rider's attempt to convert F8 into a platform-review finding.
